channel.title: Rock: Latest News, Reviews, Interviews & Videos on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in Rock: Latest News, Reviews, Interviews & Videos on Loud Legends

item.title: Spinal Tap Director ROB REINER Calls BLACK SABBATH 'Dumb' Over Stonehenge Accusation: 'It’s Ridiculous'
item.description: The director behind This Is Spinal Tap is calling out Black Sabbath for something that happened over 40 years ago, and he’s not pulling any punches. In a recent interview with Screen Rant, filmmaker Rob Reiner revisited a long-standing misunderstanding between the legendary heavy metal band and the makers of the cult comedy film.

item.title: The Legendary Musician Who Made JAMES HETFIELD Rethink His Entire Creative Process
item.description: Even after more than four decades with Metallica, James Hetfield is still learning. The frontman has spoken about what keeps him motivated creatively, crediting an unexpected influence, Elton John, with challenging the way he approaches songwriting and performance.

item.title: The AC/DC Album Fans LOVE to HATE Isn’t as BAD as You Remember
item.description: In the early 1980s, AC/DC was riding high. The back-to-back success of Highway to Hell (1979), Back in Black (1980), and For Those About to Rock (We Salute You) (1981) turned the band into a global powerhouse.

item.title: EVANESCENCE Hits No. 1 on Rock Chart for the First Time With 'Afterlife'
item.description: Evanescence has reached a major milestone. The band has scored its first-ever No. 1 song on Billboard’s Mainstream Rock Airplay chart with “Afterlife”, their latest single featured in the Netflix series Devil May Cry (watch below).

item.title: What ANGUS YOUNG Thinks About Fans Who Rejected AXL ROSE As AC/DC’s Singer
item.description: In an interview with Rolling Stone in 2021, guitarist Angus Young opened up about a moment that split fans of AC/DC, when Axl Rose stepped in as lead singer during their 2016 tour.

item.title: The AC/DC album that FLOPPED HARDER Than Expected And Nearly Turned Into A FULL-BLOWN CRISIS
item.description: Back in Black is the album everyone knows. It’s the one that sold like crazy and turned AC/DC into a global powerhouse. But not every album had the same luck.

item.title: The Genre DAVE GROHL Called 'Too Easy' And Blamed for Making ROCK DUMBER
item.description: Dave Grohl has always been a believer in loud guitars, big feelings, and not overthinking things. Foo Fighters, the band he’s fronted since the mid-’90s, built a career on that formula: simple riffs, catchy choruses, and performances that sometimes go off the rails, in a good way.

item.title: AMY LEE Talks About EMMA ANZAI Joining EVANESCENCE: 'I Called Her First'
item.description: Evanescence frontwoman Amy Lee has opened up about the band’s evolving lineup and her longtime connection with bassist Emma Anzai, offering rare insight into the decision-making behind the group’s most recent personnel shift.

item.title: EVANESCENCE's AMY LEE Joins Anti-Trump Protest in Nashville: 'Stop Kidnapping People'
item.description: Amy Lee from Evanescence was spotted at a protest in the U.S. taking a stand against Donald Trump’s immigration policies. The singer joined demonstrators in Nashville, where she lives, alongside her husband Josh Hartzler, both wearing t-shirts from the No Kings movement.

item.title: RINGO STARR Slams ROGER DALTREY Over Firing Of Son: 'Never Liked How That Little Man Runs The Band'
item.description: Zak Starkey didn’t bother hiding his disappointment after being pushed out of The Who, a gig he held for nearly 30 years as the band’s live drummer. It all unraveled after a messy show at the Royal Albert Hall earlier this year, which ultimately triggered the official announcement of his departure in April.

item.title: OnlyFans and Rock: Lorraine Lewis, The FEMME FATALE singer, embraces her wild side with new content
item.description: Lorraine Lewis isn’t just standing still. She’s moving, shaking things up, and dragging rock and roll with her (kicking and screaming, probably). You remember her, right? The voice behind FEMME FATALE.

item.title: AVENGED SEVENFOLD's M. Shadows Talks God, Purpose, and Fear
item.description: Deep in conversation on the “Artist Friendly With Joel Madden” podcast, the 43-year-old frontman for AVENGED SEVENFOLD, M. Shadows (real name: Matt Sanders), pulled no punches on religion and spirituality.

item.title: Ryan McCombs Wishes Social Media Never Existed—But He Still Uses It
item.description: Ryan McCombs—frontman of Drowning Pool and SOIL, master of growls, occasional philosopher—has thoughts about social media. Big ones. Messy ones. The kind that make you nod along until he throws in a time-travel fantasy about stopping Zuckerberg in his tracks (we’ll get there).

item.title: My Chemical Romance Drummer Bob Bryar Found Dead in Tennessee
item.description: The news of Bob Bryar’s passing feels like a gut punch to those who remember his explosive drumming during My Chemical Romance’s most iconic era. At just 44, Bryar was found dead in his Tennessee home on November 26.

item.title: Ozzy Osbourne Reacts to Jake E. Lee’s Shooting in Las Vegas
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne couldn’t hide his shock upon hearing that his former guitarist, Jake E. Lee, had been shot multiple times in Las Vegas early Tuesday morning (October 15).

item.title: Former Ozzy Osbourne Guitarist Jake E. Lee Shot in Random Attack
item.description: Guitarist Jake E. Lee, known for shredding alongside Ozzy Osbourne and his own projects like Badlands and Red Dragon Cartel, took quite an unexpected hit this week—literally. Early Tuesday, Lee was shot multiple times while out for an early morning stroll in Las Vegas.

item.title: Watch: DREAM THEATER Releases 'Night Terror' Video Ahead of 'Parasomnia' Album
item.description: February 7, 2025, marks the arrival of DREAM THEATER’s sixteenth album, “Parasomnia,” via InsideOut Music. This time, they’ve reunited with their prodigal son, drummer Mike Portnoy, whose last contribution to the band dates back to 2009’s “Black Clouds & Silver Linings.

item.title: John 5 Breaks Silence on Relationship With Rob Zombie After Joining Mötley Crüe
item.description: John 5, the guy who’s jumped from Rob Zombie’s ship straight into the glam-coated arms of Mötley Crüe, apparently hasn’t had a real chat with Zombie since his departure.

item.title: Scott Stapp Reflects on Sobriety: "Drinking is No Longer an Option"
item.description: Scott Stapp isn’t dancing around the issue of sobriety. At this point in his life, drinking is, quite simply, off the table. When asked whether it’s challenging to stay sober on something as indulgent as a cruise, particularly the band’s “Summer Of ‘99” cruises, he doesn’t hesitate: “No, it’s not.

item.title: James Hetfield: "We Don’t Want to Be a Legacy Band That Only Plays Hits"
item.description: METALLICA’s James Hetfield has made it pretty clear that they’re not interested in simply coasting on past glories. In an interview on “The Metallica Report”—that podcast where the band gives you a peek behind the curtain—James laid it out.

item.title: Korn and Adidas Pay Tribute to 1994 with New Superstar Shoes
item.description: Korn and Adidas have once again teamed up, this time with a new Superstar shoe drop. It’s about as surprising as the sun rising—anyone who’s been around long enough knows this collab was practically written in the stars.

item.title: Metallica Confirms 2025 Headline Tour with Iconic Support Acts
item.description: Metallica is rolling out a 2025 North American tour, bringing their mix of old-school riffs and new album jams to a lineup that includes Sick New World and Sonic Temple festivals.

item.title: Study Shows Korn Fans Get the Best Value for Their Tickets
item.description: These days, going to a concert is like setting fire to your wallet. Everything is overpriced, and ticket prices are no exception. But who’s ready to fork over an arm and a leg just to stand in a crowd?

item.title: Korn Showed Us the Ropes, Mötley Crüe Wanted Us Off the Stage, Says Jacoby Shaddix
item.description: Touring for over two decades brings a lot of memories—some good, some you’d rather forget. When Jacoby Shaddix and Jerry Horton of Papa Roach sat down with Q101, they didn’t hold back on sharing stories from the road.

item.title: Korn's Hits Get a Lo-Fi Makeover, And They Approve
item.description: Korn gave a nod of approval to a recent lo-fi album (listen below) of covers that takes their iconic tracks like “Freak on a Leash” and “Blind” and, let’s be honest, strips them down to something that feels like you should be sipping coffee in some indie café.

item.title: James Hetfield’s Pre-Tour Anxiety: “It’s Just Me and a Rubber Guitar”
item.description: James Hetfield of Metallica has his own brand of anxiety dreams, where his worst-case scenarios aren’t about showing up to class unprepared. No, they involve his bandmates vanishing, his guitar turning into rubber, and feeling like he’s the only one taking things seriously while everyone else is in party mode backstage.

item.title: Brian Welch on Korn's New Album: “The Heaviest in Years”
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch is dropping those familiar lines again—“heaviest stuff in years,” you know the drill. It’s almost like there’s a secret musician handbook, and on page one, right under “never say your best days are behind you,” is this classic line.

item.title: Korn's Brian Welch Introduces New Record Label XOVR Records; VIDEO
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, the guitarist from Korn, has decided that making loud noises on stage wasn’t quite enough, so he’s now entering the record label world with his latest venture, XOVR Records (that’s “Crossover Records” for those who don’t speak in mysterious abbreviations).

item.title: "Stream, Buy, or Steal": Lars Ulrich's Take on Modern Music Fans
item.description: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich once wore the crown of “public enemy” in the music scene, especially when he led the crusade against Napster and the whole file-sharing culture. Back then, he was the face of the so-called “greedy musician,” railing against the free-for-all nature of downloading that let everyone grab songs (and viruses) off the internet, slap them on a blank CD, and call it a day.

item.title: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich on Tour, Streaming Records, and Band Longevity
item.description: Lars Ulrich is no stranger to marveling at Metallica’s unlikely ride to the top. As their colossal M-72 tour rolls on, the drummer recently shared some reflections with FOX 10, and let’s just say, humility is still in the air.
